mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 1.5% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 1.5% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with the FEDFUNDS 3-month moving average (p > 0.05 in OLS).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payrolls increase exceeding 150,000 jobs accompanied by a simultaneous decline in unemployment suggests strong labor market absorption, which boosts consumer confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: In a sample of 20 post-activation windows, the 20-day forward return is not statistically different from zero (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts for two consecutive months indicates expanding credit-driven demand for equities, predicting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST month-over-month increase for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 10 activation events, the 5-day forward return mean is negative or zero (median < 0).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the Industrial Production index of more than 5% in a month signals supply-side contraction, which typically precedes a short-term S&P 500 bearish momentum over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: No significant negative relationship between INDPRO monthly changes and 20-day SPX forward returns (p > 0.1 in rolling OLS).

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2% for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to exhibit negative forward returns over the next 20 days due to market anticipation of rate hikes.
failure_condition: In 10 such inflation episodes, the 20-day forward return mean is non-negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three months, coupled with rising payrolls, creates wage pressure that supports equity valuations and predicts positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4% for 3 months and PAYEMS month-over-month increase
failure_condition: No significant positive return in 30 post-activation windows (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both retail sales and vehicle deliveries exceeding 3% each suggest resilient consumer and business demand, forecasting positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is not statistically different from the prior month's return (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling short-term rates and rising consumer confidence (measured by a composite of CPIAUCSL and HOUST), S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days tend to be positive, regardless of the direction of the rate change alone.
failure_condition: In 50 such regime windows, the 60-day forward return mean is not positive (median <= 0).
